spec.name: Earnings drift v24
spec.notes: Post-earnings drift on the reported surprise.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.7, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 2%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.72 to 2.78 (change +0.06).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.72 to 0.12. Changed by strict mode: fields eps_reported.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 2.64 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.72); it breaks even at 189.7 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.72 against 2.72 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -0.27 against 2.72 in research, a gap of +2.99.
The best year gives 17% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 84%; Sharpe is 3.41 in calm and 1.45 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.02, so the claimed 2.70 becomes 2.68 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.79 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.03, 95th percentile 0.48).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.72 to as low as 2.39 (as low as 2.46 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 21% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 13% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (pit_replay EX-2, holdout_test EX-5).
